heroLead: Orchard Mesa sits across the Colorado River from Grand Junction, fruit-growing country where irrigated orchard land has coexisted with a mostly quiet oil and gas history compared to the Piceance Basin's Garfield County core.
intro: If your family grew peaches, apples, or grapes on Orchard Mesa ground, the mineral rights you hold likely came down through that same agricultural line, kept separate from the orchard land itself as it passed through generations or eventually sold. This part of Mesa County has never seen the dense gas development found further east, so most interests here are either undrilled or tied to a single older well.

sections.heading: A flank position with limited drilling
paragraphs: The Williams Fork and Mesaverde gas-bearing formations that define Piceance Basin production do extend under parts of Mesa County, but development density around Orchard Mesa has always been much lighter than around Rifle or Parachute in Garfield County. Irrigated orchard and vineyard land also creates practical surface-use considerations that limit where a well could realistically go, even where the formation exists.

We check COGCC records for your specific section to confirm whether any well has ever produced there, since assuming based on the broader Piceance Basin reputation would misstate the real picture for most Orchard Mesa acreage.

sections.heading: What to send us
paragraphs: Your deed or legal description, plus any prior lease documents if your family has ever leased the minerals, even without a well ever being drilled. Mesa County clerk and recorder records in Grand Junction help us confirm the chain of title from there.

faqs.question: Has Orchard Mesa ever had producing gas wells?
faqs.answer: Some scattered history exists, but nowhere near the density of the Piceance core in Garfield County. We check your specific section's record before quoting.

faqs.question: Does orchard land use limit drilling here?
faqs.answer: It can, since operators generally avoid disrupting productive irrigated agricultural ground when other siting options exist, though it doesn't eliminate the possibility entirely.

faqs.question: Is it worth selling minerals that have never produced?
faqs.answer: It can be, priced as speculative rather than income-based value. We'll walk you through what that distinction means for your specific interest.

faqs.question: Does being across the river from Grand Junction change anything?
faqs.answer: Not for valuation purposes. What matters is your legal description and whatever COGCC and county records show for that specific section, regardless of which side of the Colorado River it sits on.
